desc: Formalize the greedy absorption process for a fixed K and prove that absorbing any available smaller neighbor leads to the same maximal final interval/size (exchange argument).
Design and verify the binary-lifting solution (initial draft) — found to have O(N² log N) worst-case due to inner while loops; superseded.
Design the stack-based block-merging structure (L[i], R[i] with need barriers), prove block absorbability and fixpoint uniqueness; hand-traced Sample 1 correctly.
Analyze worst-case complexity of the per-query block-jump loop — confirmed O(N²) worst case on alternating 1/2 arrays; designed binary-lifting scheme over block jumps guaranteeing O(N log N) total.

Implement the binary-lifting-over-block-jumps solution in Python (fast I/O, 64-bit-safe integers) and verify correctness against both provided samples plus edge cases (N=2, equal adjacent values, monotone arrays, alternating 1/2 pattern).
Analyze time/space complexity of the final implementation and stress-test logic against a brute-force O(N²) simulator on small random cases (by reasoning).
